I won't stage/commit — that wasn't requested. The changes are complete and verified in the working tree as-is.

## Summary

Added a queued welcome email sent after registration, without blocking the sign-up response:

- **`config/queue.ts`** / **`config/mail.ts`**: build a `QueueManager` (drivers `sync`/`redis`, selected by `QUEUE_CONNECTION`) and a `MailManager` (transports `log`/`resend`, selected by `MAIL_MAILER`, `from` sourced from `MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS`/`MAIL_FROM_NAME`) from env, and register them as the framework's global queue driver / mail manager.
- **`app/Providers/QueueProvider.ts`** / **`app/Providers/MailProvider.ts`**: thin boot-time wiring (same pattern as the existing `DatabaseProvider`), added to `src/app.ts`'s provider list.
- **`app/Mail/WelcomeMail.ts`**: a `Mail` subclass building the exact subject (`Welcome to <APP_NAME>, <name>!`) and a short plain-text greeting.
- **`app/Http/Controllers/Auth/RegisterController.ts`**: after login, does `await new WelcomeMail(mailManager, { name: user.name }).to(user.email).queue()` — this uses Guren's built-in `Mail.queue()` → `SendMailJob` mechanism, so the send is dispatched to the background queue (global driver) and only executed by the worker/sync-driver, never inline. A refused registration returns before this code runs, so nothing is queued or sent.
- **`tests/RegisterController.test.ts`**: verifies exactly one job is queued (and nothing sent) on success using `fakeQueue()`/`fakeMail()`, that running the queued work via `processJob()` sends exactly one correctly-addressed/subjected email, and that a refused registration queues/sends nothing.

Removed the unused scaffolded `app/Jobs/SendWelcomeEmailJob.ts` since the framework's built-in `SendMailJob` (triggered via `.queue()`) already provides the queue hand-off — no custom job class was needed. `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` both pass (4/4), and `bunx guren check` shows no new issues.
